1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal). Fragments:
10	`/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical (spark-lending), new
11	project, app being built, update clashed (with the app on the shell's branch
12	and a failed push), long names (an existing app to connect, no remote),
13	large project (a hundred features).
14	
15	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
16	
17	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
18	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
19	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
20	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
21	   split).
22	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
23	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
24	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
25	   real app opens the new design's page).
26	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
27	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,
28	   pull request open, nothing done yet. Stories get a state pill (Built, To
29	   build, Building) and "A change". "Also changes" is a disclosure with the
30	   full list.
31	6. **Designs show progress**: pages and how many approved or built, and when
32	   they last changed. Grouped by area, those with none (system, shell) first.
33	   A plain "Ready to build" pill when

1	// Design hosts for other stacks (plan: step 6c).
2	//
3	// A repository whose app renders its own views - another stack, or (step 8)
4	// the app a first build creates, which is its own design host - names it in a
5	// committed prelude/prelude.json:
6	//
7	//   { "host": { "start": "dotnet run --project App --urls http://localhost:5199",
8	//               "url": "http://localhost:5199", "views": ".cshtml",
9	//               "guide": "prelude/HOST.md" } }
10	//
11	// The host only renders: Prelude keeps routes, data, forms, overlays and the
12	// rest, and asks it, over HTTP, to render a view with a model inside a layout
13	// (the same job the sandboxed Eta renderer does). The contract:
14	//
15	//   GET  /__prelude/health   200 once ready
16	//   POST /__prelude/render   { root, page: { views, template, data },
17	//                              layout: { views, template, data } | { default: true, data } | null,
18	//                              regions: { <name>: { views, template, data, location } },
19	//                              query }
20	//                            -> 200 text/html, or 500 with the engine's error as text.
21	//                               A 200 may say x-prelude-ahead: <members>: state members
22	//                               a typed view's model doesn't have yet (the design is
23	//                               ahead of the app). Reported, never failed (step 7).
24	//   GET  <anything else>     the app's own static assets, at their real paths
25	//
26	// Paths in a render are relative to the repository (`root`), with forward
27	// slashes; templates have no extension (the host's is `views`). A layout of
28	// { default: true } is the host's own minimal layout. Each view sees the query
29	// as $query, and a refused form's messages as $errors in its data.
30	//
31	// A host runs a stack's views as code, unsandboxed, with this person's
32	// privileges, so it starts only once the person has approved it for this
33	// folder

Before I build this, here's what I'd do, plus two questions.

**What I have in mind:** a "Run the app" button in The app card, shown only once the app is built into main.

- It starts the app from the project's own folder (the main checkout), using the start command Prelude already uses to run the app for rendering designs (`host.start` in `prelude/prelude.json`). Then it opens the app's address in the browser.
- While the app starts, the card shows a pulse with "Starting the app…". Once it's up, the card reads "Running at `http://localhost:5199`" with **Open** and **Stop**.
- If it fails to start, the card says so and shows the last lines of the app's output.
- It isn't offered while the app is still being built, or while it only exists on the app shell's branch, because main doesn't have it yet.

**Questions:**

1. **Same address as the design host.** That command already runs the app at that address so Prelude can render designs. Running it for you would share that process, and the app may behave differently when it's run for rendering. Is it fine to share the one running app, or do you want a separate instance on its own port? A separate instance would need a second command or port in `prelude.json`.
2. **Approval.** The app runs as code on your machine, and today Prelude asks you to approve that in the design bar first. Should clicking "Run the app" count as that approval, with the button showing the exact command it will run? Or should it stay a separate step?

To change the card, I'd copy `_app` back into the design from the app's views, add a `POST /f/:project/app/run` route and its stop route, add a "running" state, and add a rule for what Run does. Shall I go ahead?
